newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on U.S. rate outlook.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on U.S. rate outlook.

text.p: Argentine bonds pushed higher in early trading Thursday, cheered by U.S. payrolls data, dealers said.

"The numbers contradict fears that the U.S. labor market is getting tighter and show that (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan did the right thing when he decided not to touch rates yesterday," a trader at a leading local bank said.
"There is also talk now the Fed won't even have to touch rates in August," he added.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 94-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.20 to 121.60.
The U.S. jobs report showed moderate wage and job growth and propelled bonds and stocks sharply higher in New York, with the long bond yield falling to 6.62 percent from 6.71 percent at the opening.
"There may be a little volatility in the local bonds market during the day, but I expect it to close with firm prices and better volume thanks to the turn of events in the U.S.," another dealer said.
